name: Home Office Checklist
description: A complete plan to set up and organize a productive, ergonomic home office.

sections.title: Choose and Set Up the Desk

items.text: Pick a desk sized to your space and tasks
Place it near a window for natural light if possible
items.note: Avoid glare on your screen by angling the desk.

items.text: Clear the surface to only what you use daily
Position the desk away from high-traffic household noise
Add a small plant or item that makes the space inviting
Test internet speed and add a wired connection if needed
Position the monitor at eye level on a riser or stand
Connect and tidy a separate keyboard and mouse
Set up a webcam and microphone for video calls
Add a power strip with surge protection for all devices
items.note: A strip with USB ports cuts down on adapters.

items.text: Stock only the supplies you use weekly within reach
Sort pens, clips, and notes into a drawer organizer
Store extra supplies in a labeled bin or nearby shelf
Add a notepad or whiteboard for quick capture
Keep a small bin for paper to recycle at the desk
Unplug everything and route cables along one path
Bundle cables with clips, sleeves, or velcro ties
Mount a power strip or tray under the desk
items.note: Lifting cables off the floor makes cleaning easier.

items.text: Label both ends of each cable for quick swaps
Set up a dedicated charging spot for phone and earbuds
Adjust the chair so feet rest flat and knees sit at ninety degrees
Support your lower back with the chair or a small cushion
Set the monitor an arm's length away at eye level
Keep elbows close to the body at about a right angle
Add a task lamp to reduce eye strain in dim light
items.note: Aim for layered lighting, not a single harsh source.

items.text: Sort existing paper into keep, scan, shred, and recycle
Set up labeled folders for active and reference documents
Scan important papers and back up the files securely
Create a simple naming system for digital files
Schedule a weekly reset to clear and refile the desk
items.note: Five minutes on Friday keeps Monday calm.

faq.q: What do I need to set up a home office?
faq.a: Start with a desk, a supportive chair, reliable internet, and good lighting, then add the tech and supplies your work requires. Build from those essentials before adding extras.

faq.q: How do I make my home office ergonomic?
faq.a: Position the monitor at eye level an arm's length away, keep elbows and knees at roughly ninety degrees, and support your lower back. Good posture prevents strain over long workdays.

faq.q: How can I set up a home office in a small space?
faq.a: Use a compact or wall-mounted desk, go vertical with shelves, and pick a chair that tucks away. A corner or closet nook can become a full workspace with smart storage.

faq.q: How do I keep my home office organized?
faq.a: Give every item a home, manage cables, and clear your desk at the end of each day. A simple filing system and a weekly reset keep paper and clutter from piling up.

faq.q: Can I print this home office checklist?
faq.a: Yes. Download the printable PDF, keep it at your desk, and check off each task as you set up and organize your workspace from desk to filing.
